record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: How does exchange magnetic anisotropy, including anisotropy associated with surface oxidization and magnetic proximity, affect magnetoresistance, spin-orbit torque switching, spin Seebeck response, anomalous Nernst response, and optical control in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures that are being proposed for spintronics, opto-spintronics, spin-caloritronics, and related devices?

evidence.quote: We highlight below the important effects that MP-mediated exchange magnetic anisotropy may have on spin configurations, spin-transport, thermo-spin-transport, and valleytronic properties of 2D van der Waals magnet-based heterostructures, which are open to a wide range of important technological applications (Fig. 11).
In particular, oxidized Fe3GeTe2 has been shown to exhibit the EB effect [61], and the effect that exchange anisotropy may have on the MR and SOT should be investigated systematically.

This important observation reveals a new perspective for optically controlling SV and SOT effects in Fe3GeTe2-based heterostructures or similar vdW heterostructures at room temperature, which has the potential to establish a new subfield of opto-spintronics. Future studies are needed to realize all of this.

It is likely that both SSE and ANE coexist in Fe3GeTe2, but no study has been made to decouple their relative contributions. In SSE and ANE systems, surface/interface magnetic anisotropy has been shown to play an important role [139][140].

artifact.category_tag: van der Waals magnetic heterostructures and exchange bias
artifact.status_search_result: Research on exchange bias and interfacial anisotropy effects on magnetoresistance, spin-orbit-torque switching, spin Seebeck/anomalous Nernst response, and optical control in 2D vdW magnetic heterostructures (notably Fe3GeTe2-based systems) is active, with partial experimental progress on individual effects but no systematic quantitative theory linking exchange anisotropy (from oxidation and magnetic proximity) to all of these device responses. The question remains broadly open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Open Questions and Perspectives review identifying systematic investigation of exchange anisotropy effects on MR, SOT, SSE, ANE, and optical control as needed future work.
status_evidence.claim: The cited problems are framed as open perspectives requiring future systematic study.
